title: Multi-Actor Shared Algorithms (SRP Accidental Duplication)
pattern: Sharing a common utility function between methods serving entirely different actors or departments to avoid writing duplicate code structures.
why_bad: It couples distinct actors to each other's evolutionary paths. If the CFO's team decides that overtime calculation should change (e.g., regular hours capped at 37.5), a developer altering the shared `regular_hours` helper will silently corrupt the report numbers used by the COO's team, causing major reporting errors.
detection: A private helper method called by multiple public methods that are specified by or responsible to different actors (e.g., different organizational roles).
counterexample: Low-level algorithmic primitives (e.g., hashing or serialization) where the operation is fully technical and does not depend on organizational actor requirements.
